commentary_title: LR1 demand remains resilient as rising vessel availability caps market tightness
commentary_summary: LR1 tonne-mile demand remained supportive, with the tonne-mile index at 107.6, up 4.5% YoY, suggesting resilient long-haul product flows despite softer market conditions. However, utilisation fell to 88.9%, down 2.5 percentage points MoM and 3.4 percentage points YoY, suggesting vessel supply growth and improving fleet productivity are outpacing demand gains. | Vessel availability increased across key trading regions, with anchored capacity declining by 9.9% MoM in the west and 23.7% MoM in the east. The share of laden vessels rose by 8.2 percentage points in the west, reflecting healthy cargo activity, but higher ballast speeds in both regions indicate prompt tonnage remains readily available as owners reposition vessels more aggressively. | Market tightness continued to ease as congestion levels moderated and voyage turnaround improved. Lower anchorage volumes, coupled with a rise in sailing speeds despite bunker prices increasing to $866 per tonne, effectively expanded the active fleet supply. As a result, strong tonne-mile demand and cargo movements provided support to LR1 earnings, but growing vessel availability limited the scope for a sustained rate rally.
